thread:
Maya: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a thin 'normalize' shim at the gateway that upgrades v1 payloads to v2 on the fly. opt-in per-tenant, telemetry + QA flag. low-risk path for customers that can't update clients immediately
Otto: high-level: sound approach. main concern is perf and the cognitive load of two codepaths in gateway
Maya: agree on perf. the shim would be intentionally tiny: header sniff -> transform -> forward. no state, no KV cache touches. target < 1ms p50 extra latency in our staging tests
Ben: do we have example transforms? sometimes v1 had array-of-ops vs v2 single-object. need canonical mapping rules
Maya: yes, attached mapping doc (short):

- v1: {"ops": [{"op":"generate","prompt":"..."}], "meta": {..}}
- v2: {"request": {"type":"generate","prompt":"..."}, "trace": {"client_version":"v1"}}

Maya: shim does: pick first op, coerce types, drop deprecated fields, attach X-Compat-Source header
Sara: how do we opt tenants in/out? feature flag service or tenant config?
Otto: tenant config so SRE can toggle fast. also add a TTL for opt-in so we can nudge customers to migrate
Ben: telemetry needed: count of transformed requests, errors, and a small sample of transformed payloads (scrubbed). must not log PII
Maya: agreed. plan: metric names: compat.normalize.count, compat.normalize.errors, compat.normalize.sample (scrubbed)
deploy-bot: deploy queued: gateway/normalize-shim v1.0 -> staging (triggered by @Maya) :rocket:
Otto: failure modes: what if the transform incorrectly drops a field and changes model choice? need safety net - propagate original request in trace so we can replay
Maya: we'll include original SHA256 in span and ability to fetch raw request from short-lived archive (7 days) for debug. access controls enforced
Ben: rollback story? If we see error spike we should 1) flip tenant opt-out 2) automatically route new traffic to v2-only path 3) create alert channel - maybe #incidents
Sara: also consider graceful degradation: if transform fails for a request, gateway should 1) attempt passthrough to v1 backend (if still available) OR 2) return 400 with clear message and suggest client upgrade. which is less disruptive?
Otto: prefer passthrough while v1 backend is alive. fallback to 400 only when v1 path removed. but we need throttles to avoid overload loops
Maya: agree. plan: primary: transform->v2 path, fallback: passthrough to v1 backend. add circuit-breaker thresholds: 5xx rate > 2% or latency spike -> cut opt-in for all tenants
Ben: will this affect logs/traces? we must indicate that request was normalized and which rules applied. maybe header "X-Redwood-Normalized: rules=v1->v2;rule=ops-first"
Maya: yes will add X-Redwood-Normalized + X-Redwood-Compat: v1 to traces. also emit a debug span when sample tracing enabled
Sara: security check: any chance the shim could be used to bypass auth scopes or change tenant id? important to assert transform cannot modify auth fields and we validate tenant from token, not payload
Maya: critical point — shim will not touch auth headers or token. tenant id comes from token introspection; payload fields that look like tenant are dropped before transform
Otto: testing plan? unit tests for each rule, e2e with canary tenants, load test to ensure <1ms overhead @ p50 and <10ms p99
Maya: propose rollout: 1) deploy shim disabled 2) enable sampling (0.1%) to observe transforms 3) opt-in internal tenants 4) expand to canary customers (5%) 5) 30-day observation 6) broad opt-in waves with customer comms
Ben: add a migration webhook: when we opt a customer out due to errors, webhook to their account owner so we can coordinate upgrades
Sara: are we adding a long-term plan to remove shim? timeline should be explicit: shim slated for removal 12 months after stable opt-in plateau; if adoption < 80% we revisit
Maya: milestone: remove point — target 12mo, but will maintain backstop flags for enterprise customers beyond that on case-by-case basis
Otto: tiny nit: name the feature flag compat.gateway.normalize not gateway.normalize to be explicit about boundary
Maya: noted. final checklist before staging deploy: mapping doc updated, telemetry dashboards, circuit-breaker thresholds set, rollout playbook written, security review sign-off
Ben: lgtm pending staging metrics
Sara: +1 on playbook, please include sample customer comms language (we can reuse the migration template)
Maya: will draft comms and the playbook. thanks everyone
deploy-bot: deployed: gateway/normalize-shim v1.0 -> staging at 2024-04-18T15:12:30Z
Maya: tagging @eng-sre and @support for visibility and to prepare runbook
Otto: leaving follow-up item: schedule 60m post-deploy review next week to validate perf numbers
Maya: done. calendar invite sent. :calendar:
